title: Permutations
prompt:
Given an array `nums` of distinct integers, return all possible permutations of the array, in any order.

For deterministic comparison, sort the outer list of permutations (for example, by converting each permutation to a tuple and sorting the list of tuples).

examples.explanation: With a single element, there's only one possible ordering.

constraints: All integers in nums are unique
hints: A permutation is built by picking one unused element at a time until none remain. Track which elements have already been placed in the current path.
Use backtracking: at each recursive call, try every element not yet used, add it to the current path, mark it used, recurse, then undo (remove it, mark unused) before trying the next.

When the current path's length equals len(nums), you've built a complete permutation — record a copy of it. Sort the final list of permutations (e.g. by tuple conversion) for deterministic comparison.

solution.approach: Standard backtracking over 'used' state. Maintain a boolean array marking which indices of nums have already been placed into the current path. At each recursive call, if the path length equals len(nums), a full permutation is complete, so record a copy. Otherwise, try every index not yet used: mark it used, append its value to the path, recurse, then backtrack by removing it and marking it unused again. After collecting every permutation, sort the outer list (via tuple conversion) so the result is deterministic regardless of generation order.
solution.code:
def permute(nums):
    n = len(nums)
    result = []
    path = []
    used = [False] * n

    def backtrack():
        if len(path) == n:
            result.append(path[:])
            return
        for i in range(n):
            if used[i]:
                continue
            used[i] = True
            path.append(nums[i])
            backtrack()
            path.pop()
            used[i] = False

    backtrack()
    result.sort(key=lambda perm: tuple(perm))
    return result
solution.spaceComplexity: O(n * n!) for the output, O(n) recursion depth
